payload.posture: Read Ezekiel 37:1–14 as one movement in the resurrection, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states ezekiel sees dry bones receive sinews, flesh, breath, and life; the vision is then identified with Israel’s lost hope and a promise of opened graves, Spirit, land, and restored life. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of the resurrection.
